clue.text: Place to keep one good plug

indicators.note: a place that keeps something holds it within, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: a spot is a place
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone recommends a spot to store a good stopper or bung.
explanation.definitionFit: A tap or bung that stops the flow from a cask is called a plug or stopper.

clue.text: Sort of deal cards on time

parts.note: a pack is a set of playing cards
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A card dealer deals the pack promptly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' looks like a card game term, but it is part of the definition, a kind of agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A package deal is an agreement covering several items or conditions bundled together.

clue.text: Sort out right measurement for trousers?

indicators.note: sorting out the letters of right puts them into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A tailor is told to get the trouser size correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Waist size, the distance around the middle, is the measurement a pair of trousers must fit.

clue.text: Step across certain to be appreciated

indicators.note: one piece across another spans it, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: a tread is a step, as on a staircase
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Someone steps confidently, sure they'll be valued.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prized and valued highly is cherished, much appreciated.

clue.text: Free trader should cover empty college houses like this

indicators.note: one piece covering another sits around it, so the other letters go inside
freeing the letters of trader lets them fall into a new order
an empty word keeps only its outside letters, the first and last of college

explanation.surface: A trader with no ties ought to insure the bare student halls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' looks like an adjective for the trader but signals the anagram (TERRAD); 'should cover' wraps that around the two letters left by 'empty'.
explanation.definitionFit: Houses built joined in a continuous row are described as being in a terrace.

clue.text: Bit of grass scouts lost on summit of Kilimanjaro

indicators.note: scouts who are lost are scrambled and out of order
the summit of a word is its top, the first letter of Kilimanjaro

explanation.surface: Scouts climbing Kilimanjaro lose their way near the top amid clumps of grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' makes TUSSOC from SCOUTS; 'summit of' gives K.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuft or clump of coarse grass growing in a dense mound is a small patch of it.

clue.text: Hears about birds unable to fly

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of hears are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone learns of flightless birds.
explanation.definitionFit: These large South American ratites, like ostriches, cannot fly.

clue.text: Husband leaving chain rattling in fruit machine

indicators.note: in places the shaken letters within the fruit

parts.note: an apple is a fruit

indicators.note: rattling shakes the remaining letters of chain into a new order
the husband leaving means his letter is taken out

explanation.surface: A husband walks out as the chain rattles inside a fruit machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fruit machine', British for a slot machine, reads as one phrase but splits: fruit gives the outer word, machine is the definition. 'rattling' makes IANC from what remains after 'leaving'.
explanation.definitionFit: A household device such as a washing machine or fridge is a domestic machine.

clue.text: Regularly repair rugs, finding bugs

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of repair, from the second

parts.note: rug is slang for a wig or hairpiece

explanation.surface: Someone mending carpets finds insects in them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' gives EAR from repair. 'rugs' looks like the carpets but means hairpieces.
explanation.definitionFit: These small insects with pincers at the tail are crawling creepy-crawlies, colloquially bugs.

clue.text: Cleaner range kept by nameless woodworker

indicators.note: something kept by another is held inside it, so these letters go within
nameless means without N, the abbreviation for name

parts.note: a carpenter works with wood
a sweep is a range or extent, as in the broad sweep of a view

explanation.surface: An anonymous joiner keeps a cooker or a stretch of hills in his workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nameless' drops N, the usual abbreviation for name, leaving CARPETER, which 'kept by' wraps around the range.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-pushed device with rotating brushes for floor coverings is a household cleaning tool.

clue.text: Male ego of Scot confronting his doctor

indicators.note: confronting means facing, so the Scot comes first and the rest follow

parts.note: Mac is a familiar name for a Scotsman
MO is a Medical Officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A Scotsman squares up to his GP, his manly pride bruised.
explanation.definitionFit: Exaggerated masculine pride and assertiveness is a Spanish-derived word for macho swagger.

clue.text: Short temper

definitions.meaning: a short is a small measure of strong liquor such as whisky
temper as in mettle or disposition, a person's character or mood

explanation.surface: Two words describing a quick-tempered person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short temper' reads as one phrase, but it is two separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Whisky or gin served as a short is a distilled drink; and temper or mettle is one's courage or disposition.

clue.text: Recall ignoring case of role for elected representative

indicators.note: ignoring something leaves it out, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: to recall is to remember

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, the first and last letters of role

explanation.surface: Someone forgets the outline of a part played by a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' gives R and E from role; 'ignoring' removes them from REMEMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: An MP is a Member of Parliament, a politician chosen by voters to sit in the House.

clue.text: Charges on skips for such retail outlets

parts.note: police book a suspect when they charge them
hops are small skips or jumps

explanation.surface: Shops pay fees for hiring skips, the big rubbish containers used in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Shops selling printed volumes are a kind of retail outlet; the answer's own pieces show which kind.

clue.text: Generosity of types accepting needs intermittently

indicators.note: something accepting another takes it in, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: kinds are types or sorts

indicators.note: intermittently means every other letter of needs, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Charitable people of various sorts take in those in need now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intermittently' takes the first, third and fifth letters of needs; 'accepting' places them before the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Being open-handed and considerate to others is a quality of warmth and goodwill.

clue.text: Supplier of fresh green nuts ignoring us

parts.note: new means fresh
sage is a grey-green colour

indicators.note: ignoring something leaves it out, so those letters are removed from nuts

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grocer sells fresh green nuts but leaves us out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' takes US out of nuts to leave NT. A British corner shop selling papers is the supplier meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper who sells newspapers and magazines supplies the daily press to customers.

clue.text: Arrange again to incorporate first of cases for part-time judge

indicators.note: to incorporate is to take inside, so the letter goes within the other piece

parts.note: to reorder is to arrange again

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, C of cases

explanation.surface: A court clerk re-sorts the files so the leading case goes to the stand-in judge.
explanation.definitionFit: In England and Wales a Recorder is a barrister or solicitor sitting as a judge only some of the time.

clue.text: Obscure European Community borders with Spain

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Community
lips are edges or borders, as of a cup
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: The EC's frontiers with Spain are hard to make out.
explanation.definitionFit: To overshadow or hide something from view, as the moon does the sun, is to obscure it.

clue.text: Begrudges lack of parking in awards

indicators.note: a lack of something means it is missing, so that letter is removed

parts.note: presents are awards or gifts
P is the symbol for parking

explanation.surface: A driver resents prize-giving where there is nowhere to park.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel bitter or aggrieved about something is to grudge it.

clue.text: Wife gives aid to impudent youths

parts.note: to help is to give aid to

explanation.surface: A wife assists some cheeky young people.
explanation.definitionFit: Whelp, literally a puppy, is a dismissive term for a cheeky boy or young lad.

clue.text: Indication of complex protein

indicators.note: complex means intricate or tangled, so the letters of protein are mixed up

explanation.surface: A sign that a protein molecule is complicated.
explanation.definitionFit: A hint or clue that shows the way is a sign or indication.

clue.text: Shut as result of muggy day

parts.note: close weather is muggy, warm and airless

explanation.surface: Something was shut down because of the humid weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Shut and the answer are synonyms, as of a door or a shop not open.

clue.text: Go on and on in given order travelling north

indicators.note: travelling north says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone keeps talking, in the set sequence, while heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Go' as the definition and left 'in' unexplained; 'Go on and on' is the definition and 'in' signals the hidden letters. In a down clue, 'travelling north' reads them upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak tediously in a monotonous tone, like a bee's hum, is to ramble on endlessly.

clue.text: Substitutes put up with error

parts.note: to stand something is to put up with it
a sin is a wrongdoing or error

explanation.surface: Replacements are tolerated despite their mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy who takes another's place temporarily is said to fill in or cover for them.

clue.text: Hope to have drive and energy in the morning

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for Drive in addresses
E is the symbol for energy
a.m. means in the morning

explanation.surface: Someone wishes for motivation and pep first thing in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambition or aspiration one longs to achieve is a hope.

clue.text: Statement church intended for broadcast by me, for example

parts.note: me is an example of a pronoun
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard, so the word is taken as it sounds

parts.note: meant is to have intended

explanation.surface: A speaker says a church announcement was meant for him to read out on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for broadcast' turns MEANT into its sound-alike MENT; 'me, for example' is a grammar class, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal declaration or announcement made publicly is an official statement.

clue.text: Make another judgement about girls going topless in front of son

indicators.note: in front of means this piece comes just before the next

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: going topless means losing the top, here the first letter

parts.note: lasses are girls

explanation.surface: A scandal: young women bare their tops before a young man, prompting second thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going topless' takes L off LASSES, leaving ASSES; 'about' looks attached to the definition but gives RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaluate a matter again is to make a fresh appraisal of it.

clue.text: Quality of magazine about Britain

indicators.note: about means around, so the magazine goes around the other letters

parts.note: Time is a well-known American news magazine

explanation.surface: A review of a magazine's standard of writing about Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Tone colour, the character of a sound distinct from pitch and volume, is a musical quality.
